result.title: Rènyi-Regularized Flow-Based Variational Inference for Bayesian Calibration
result.summary: Variational inference with normalizing flows provides a flexible posterior approximation for Bayesian model calibration, but struggles when the posterior has several modes separated by regions of low probability mass. We study this behavior in a two-parameter twin experiment and regularize the variational objective. Under Gaussian observation errors and a Gaussian prior, the corresponding minimization objective is the expected Tikhonov calibration objective minus the differential entropy of the approximating distribution. However, the expected Tikhonov term favors concentration near one of the modes, while entropy maximization does not guarantee multimodality. We introduce a regularization term based on Rényi divergence that encourages the approximate posterior to cover the prior support. In the connected bimodal case, a flow approximation represents both modes; in the case with well-separated modes, the flow and Gaussian mixture frequently miss one mode. The introduced regularization reduces the near-collapse fraction from 50% to 25%. While the regularization improves mode coverage in this experiment, it changes the Bayesian variational objective, introduces a trade-off in approximation accuracy, and does not provide a general solution to mode collapse.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究贝叶斯模型校准中 normalizing flow 变分推断遇到多峰后验时容易只覆盖单个模态的问题，提出基于 Rényi 散度的正则项鼓励近似后验覆盖先验支撑集，并在双参数孪生实验中把近塌缩比例从 50% 降到 25%，同时说明该正则改变原变分目标、带来精度权衡且并非通用解法。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「多峰覆盖」问题与「近塌缩比例」度量，可能可供核查 LVR 中多种 latent 假设是否被保留及如何评价覆盖度，但领域相隔较远，仅为概念与评价层面的启发。
